Content Advisory: Death of a fictional character Age Recommendation: All ages A part of our Main Stage Series A STAGED CONCERT collaboration with Metropolis School of Performing Arts and JAM Orchestra. What is a staged concert? The orchestra is on stage, fully visible to the audience. To be able to see as well as hear the players in these timeless productions is a truly thrilling experience. Will the actors be in character? Absolutely. They will inhabit their roles completely, and there might be some quite physical staging. There is certainly no less drama than in a fully staged production. Are there costumes, props and set pieces? Yes, and no. Sometimes the actors will be in full costume, and sometimes the designers make use of cleverly symbolic elements. There is also use of dramatic lighting and with the new projectors purchased with money raised from our Fund-A-Cause at our 2026 Gala, we will be able to offer a grander visual experience during these stagings. Why a staged concert? It all began for a practical reason – when collaborating with a full orchestra, it is simply not possible to fit them in and out of sight in the usual ways on a stage of our size. However, we couldn’t let that stop us from programming these incredible works, so we found a new way to do it that allows us to really let the music shine in a way that has become increasingly rare in the world of theatre today. ABOUT THE SHOW Ariel, a young mermaid, is itching to explore beyond the boundaries of her father King Triton’s watery kingdom. Admiring her collection of human goods, Ariel daydreams of emerging onto the surface, walking on land, and meeting the strange human she saw sailing by. Meanwhile, Ursula – Triton’s sister – dreams about her own plans to overthrow King Triton. When a storm throws Prince Eric overboard his ship and Ariel saves his life, Triton is enraged, and destroys her precious collection of human detritus. Ariel, distraught and furious at her father, is conned by the scheming Ursula and agrees to sacrifice her voice in exchange for her land legs – but only for three days, during which time she must kiss Prince Eric, or else become Ursula’s captive forever. For three days, Ariel attempts to prove to Eric her love for him, but without her voice, she falls short. Ursula returns, dragging Ariel back into the depths of the sea, but not before revealing that she killed Ariel’s mother. Ariel destroys the shell that harnesses Ursula’s power, thereby destroying Ursula completely. King Triton realizes that his daughter does have the power to choose her own destiny, and grants her back her human form, where she is reunited with the Prince. items.detail: Purchase Tickets Tuesday, February 9th, 2027: 7:30pm Tickets: $40 ABOUT THE SHOW: Creole Stomp has captured the ears and the feet of Louisiana music fans across North America. Led by French-speaking Creole fiddler and accordionist Dennis Stroughmatt, Creole Stomp keeps listeners enthralled and dancers moving on the floor with a rollicking mix of contemporary blues, swamp pop, and traditional Cajun and zydeco dance tunes. Creole Stomp shows have become legendary for the heart and passion conveyed from the stage—music with emotion and energy that literally jumps from the band. In fact, over the years the band has become informally known as “The Grateful Dead of Creole Music,” for their well-oiled, dancer-driven, crowd-pleasing marathon jams and improvisation. Traditional Louisiana Cajun two-steps, reels, and waltzes sizzle in the stew along with Creole blues and mazurkas. A favorite on the Cajun-zydeco dance circuit, the band has also become a celebrated fixture at concert halls around the United States, ranging from outdoor parks and theaters to folk and blues festivals. No matter the venue, wherever they come from, and wherever they go, Creole Stomp is a band that knows how to throw a Louisiana party!

items.detail: Purchase Tickets Monday, March 8th, 2027: 7:30 PM Tickets: $25 ABOUT THE SHOW: METHTACULAR! is Steven Strafford’s hilarious, harrowing, and ultimately hopeful autobiographical solo show about addiction, survival, and the long road back to oneself. Using outrageous stories, original songs, and unflinching honesty, Strafford recounts the three years he spent addicted to crystal meth while pursuing an acting career in Chicago. Moving between sharp comedy and painful revelation, METHTACULAR! explores the lies we tell others, the lies we tell ourselves, and the unexpected grace of getting another chance. It is a fiercely funny and deeply human celebration of recovery and the stubborn instinct to survive. ABOUT THE TEAM: STEVEN STRAFFORD (Playwright/Performer) is an actor, playwright, director, and educator whose award-winning autobiographical solo show, METHTACULAR!, has been performed across the country and was recorded live at Steppenwolf Theatre in 2019. His plays include SMALL JOKES ABOUT MONSTERS, published and licensed by Dramatists Play Service; GREATER ILLINOIS, which premiered at TheatreWorks@TheSquare in Memphis; and THE MATCH GAME, which received its world premiere at Ensemble Theatre Cincinnati. His TYA musical HANSEL AND GRETL: OFF THE GRID will premiere at Marriott Theatre in 2027. His work has also been developed at regional theatres and universities across the country. As an actor, Steven has appeared at theatres including Goodman Theatre, Marriott Theatre, Drury Lane Theatre, and Steppenwolf Theatre. He has played men, women, rivers, frogs, birds, and many people with mustaches. He currently serves as Head of the BFA Musical Theatre program at Ohio University. ADAM FITZGERALD (Director) is a director, filmmaker, writer, and content creator whose work has been recognized with an Emmy Nomination, “Critic’s Picks” from The New York Times, The Chicago Tribune, TimeOut Chicago and TimeOut New York, “Best of the Year” nods in The Advocate Magazine and The Contra Costa Times, a Jeff Award Nomination, and San Francisco Bay Area Critics Award nominations. His PSA “Think Before You Speak” (director/writer) for GLSEN won a national contest judged by Brett Ratner and The Ad Council (and screened at the LA Respect Awards) and his short film, OCCUPY ME (director/writer), was an official selection screening in multiple festivals across Europe, Asia, and North America. Adam directed RESISTANCE RADIO for MAN IN THE HIGH CASTLE (Amazon Studios, Campfire) which was nominated for an Emmy Award and received two Silver and three Bronze Lions at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity.

items.detail: Purchase Tickets April 3rd, 2027: 2:00pm & 7:30pm Tickets: $45 ABOUT THE SHOW: The Neverly Brothers concerts take you on a guided musical VIRTUAL TOUR of the birth, near-death, and resurrection of rock n’ roll – from 1955 to 1965. You’ll learn rock history and be thoroughly entertained with their chronological song sequence, stories behind the music, and vintage wardrobe changes. Their energetic stage show features show-stopping renditions of early hits by Jerry Lee Lewis, Chuck Berry, Buddy Holly, The Beatles, the Rolling Stones, and more! The first half of their concert pays tribute to the music created by the 1950s American Rock n’ Roll pioneers – which by 1960 had become a distant memory but became the inspiration for the next wave of young rock bands from Britain. The second half pays tribute to the 1964 British Invasion bands that re-recorded forgotten 1950s American rock music, along with lesser-known early 1960s rhythm & blues songs, recorded their own original songs, and pulled Rock’n’ Roll from the edge of extinction by reinventing and re-energizing it for a new generation. Their repertoire includes spirited performances of classics like “Great Balls of Fire,” “Johnny B. Goode,” “Wake Up Little Susie,” “Summertime Blues,” “That’ll Be The Day,” “Twist & Shout,” “Roll Over Beethoven,” “Satisfaction,” “You Really Got Me,” “Love Potion #9,” and many more! It‘s not “moldy oldies” – it’s “old-school cool!” So hop aboard our virtual tour bus and fasten your seatbelts for an exciting MAGICAL HISTORY TOUR!

Content Advisory: death of a fictional character Age Recommendation: All ages ABOUT THE SHOW On a farm in the countryside, a barn is full of typical farm animals – some chatty geese, a gluttonous rat, and a humble spider perched in her corner web. But Wilbur the pig, the runt of the litter who was saved by the kind farm girl Fern, is all alone and awaiting a frightening fate. Luckily, he befriends the wise spider, Charlotte, who decides to use all her wits to help save Wilbur’s life. By writing out messages in her web, Charlotte tricks the farmer, who believes the messages are being written by Wilbur. He enters Wilbur into the county fair’s Best Pig competition, where Wilbur has to prove his skill. Charlotte, now old and tired, decides to sacrifice everything to help Wilbur one final time. Though Wilbur cannot return the favor to Charlotte, he ensures that her legacy will live on.
items.title: Charlotte's Web
